course_description.character: Latest official route reference (2026; not yet confirmed for 2027): an island-wide paved road circuit out of Punat on Krk, one of Croatia's largest Adriatic islands (second-largest after Cres). The 82km route ran north from Punat through Krk town, Malinska, Njivice and Omišalj, cut inland through the karst villages of Dobrinj and Vrbnik, climbed to Treskavac Pass, descended into Baška on the island's south coast, then turned back over a 7.9km climb toward Punat. Four categorized ascents broke up otherwise rolling terrain.
course_description.signature_challenge: Latest 2026 route reference: the Vrbnik-side climb to Treskavac Pass, immediately followed by the long descent into Baška. The 2027 course is pending.
suffering_zones: Km 52.2: 3.1km at 5.8% (Category 3), also the relative-cutoff control point
Km 67.0: 7.9km at 3.6% (Category 3) — the return climb toward Punat

history.origin_story: Inaugural edition held in Punat on April 27, 2024, organized by Hoteli Punat/Falkensteiner Punat with support from the Punat Tourist Board; Marin Kirin and Toni Dujmenović have directed the race since. Run with the Croatian Cycling Federation and Granfondo World Tour, though it is not a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier.
history.reputation: A young but quickly-sold-out event — the 2026 field cap was reached about six weeks before race day.

biased_opinion.verdict: Real, Young, Popular — But Read the Fine Print
biased_opinion.summary: The organizer's embedded RaceResult event confirms the fourth Krk Gran Fondo for Saturday, April 24, 2027, with a 600-rider allocation. Sources for 2026 variously report 400 actual starters, roughly 450 expected riders, and a 500-place registration allocation, so historical field reporting remains inconsistent. The published 2026 course is a rolling-island circuit with four categorized climbs and a Treskavac-to-Baška high point, not a flat coastal cruise, but the organizer has not yet published a 2027-specific course or rulebook. The 2026 paperwork also has real document-control problems: its propositions PDF misprints the year, inconsistently rounds the distance, and carries over a stray Zadar reference. Treat April 24 as confirmed and the course details as provisional until 2027 documents replace the 2026 material.
strengths: The organizer-linked RaceResult event confirms Saturday, April 24, 2027, with a 600-rider allocation
Rolling-island course with four categorized climbs and a Treskavac Pass high point
Post-race coverage reports extensive road control and a 190-person event operating team
Adriatic island route through Malinska, Njivice, Omišalj, Dobrinj, Vrbnik and Baška
weaknesses: Official race-propositions PDF has real document-control problems (wrong year printed, distance rounding inconsistencies, a leftover Zadar reference) — don't take the PDF as gospel over the live event page
Riders 40+ minutes behind the leader at the km-52 control are diverted to a shortened finish — stricter than typical recreational-fondo pacing
Not a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier, unlike nearby Istria Gran Fondo — lower competitive prestige
Young event (3rd edition in 2026) with a correspondingly thin track record
Organizer's own field-size reporting is inconsistent (400 vs. ~450 vs. 500 across different materials)
biased_opinion.bottom_line: The April 24, 2027 race date is confirmed. The island-road character is established, but wait for the 2027 course and rules before treating the historical 82 km distance or km-52 cutoff as current.

final_verdict.one_liner: A young Krk Island road race with a confirmed April 24, 2027 date and an edition-specific course still pending.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Keep it on the calendar if a compact Adriatic island road race appeals to you, but wait for the 2027 course and rulebook before making route-specific pacing or equipment decisions. The 82 km distance, four categorized climbs, and relative cutoff describe the completed 2026 edition only.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer, UCI-qualifying Croatian gran fondo: Istria Gran Fondo (Umag, 105km, UCI Gran Fondo World Series). For another Adriatic island event: Granfondo Pag - Cycling on the Moon (Novalja, ~107km/1,210m).
